accepted.question_text: For an ideal incompressible inviscid fluid in a fixed domain M whose boundary may contain sources and sinks, can one give a variational, preferably geodesic, formulation of the motion? What boundary data, exterior forces, or memory variables must be included so that the formulation covers examples such as a pipe with inflow and outflow?
accepted.context_brief: Ideal fluids with sources and sinks

accepted.question_text: For fluid or material systems modeled by Lie groupoids rather than Lie groups, can the geodesic and Hamiltonian descriptions of Euler-Arnold equations on Lie groupoids be extended to elasticity theory?

For the Lie groupoid of multiphase or generalized volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, equipped with the source-wise right-invariant L2 metric whose geodesics describe multiphase Euler flows, can one describe its differential geometry, including sectional curvature, Ricci curvature, and conjugate points, analogously to Arnold's geometry of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group D_mu(M)?

Can Arnold's geodesic framework be extended from the diffeomorphism group D(M) to the semigroup of maps Map(M) so that it describes both smooth solutions of Burgers-like or compressible fluid equations and their continuations after shock formation?

For material particles moving in R^d with d>1 that stick on collision, can one find a variational description that covers both potential and non-potential fluid flows and is flexible enough to model formation and evolution of shock waves for the multidimensional Burgers equation?

Can one construct a mechanical or fluid model whose configuration space is the group D_mu(M) of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and whose energy metric is a left-invariant L2 metric? Are there physically interesting systems exhibiting that left invariance?
For the incompressible Euler equations, is the Cauchy problem ill-posed in the Besov spaces B^1_{infty,q} for 1<q<infty, the range between B^1_{infty,1} and the Zygmund space B^1_{infty,infty}?

Let M be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold and let phi be a volume-preserving diffeomorphism of M of Sobolev class H^s. Does the global two-point boundary-value problem hold: can one find a divergence-free vector field v in H^s(M) with exp_e(v)=phi, and can one find a curve gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M) from the identity e to phi minimizing the L2 energy integral?

For two-dimensional hydrodynamics on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, does the action functional associated with the L2 kinetic-energy metric satisfy the Palais-Smale compactness condition?
If M is a compact surface of genus at least 2, or a multiconnected bounded domain in R^2 with at least two holes, does D_mu^s(M) contain a closed geodesic for the L2 hydrodynamic metric?
accepted.context_brief: Closed geodesics in fluid configuration space

accepted.question_text: How far is D_mu(M), the Frechet Lie group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms with the right-invariant L2 hydrodynamic metric, from being an infinite-dimensional locally symmetric Riemannian space?

For ideal incompressible Euler flows, are particle trajectories analytic functions of time in all spatial dimensions, and for manifolds with boundary how does this time-analyticity depend on whether the boundary is analytic?

For Yudovich solutions of the Euler equations, where the velocity field is divergence-free and has bounded vorticity curl u, are particle trajectories analytic in time? If only Gevrey regularity is known, is that Gevrey regularity sharp?

For partially analytic functions, meaning functions whose level lines are real analytic even though the function may have only finite Sobolev regularity across levels, what natural mathematical structure should replace the vector-space structure that fails under addition?

For every compact analytic two-dimensional Riemannian manifold M with analytic boundary, is the set GM(M) of generalized minimal flows a nonempty proper subset of the Yudovich space YU(M), where YU(M) consists of divergence-free vector fields with bounded vorticity?
For every generalized minimal flow u(x,t) in two-dimensional Euler dynamics, are all level lines of the vorticity curl u(x,t)=constant real analytic?
For every generalized minimal flow whose vorticity domain decomposes numerically into blobs B_1,...,B_N and a background region B_0, is curl u constant on the background B_0?
Can nonstationary generalized minimal flows in two-dimensional Euler dynamics have dynamics more complicated than time-periodic or quasiperiodic motion, for example chaotic behavior?

Can one define anisotropic function spaces for ideal hydrodynamics that encode higher smoothness along flow lines, and prove existence and uniqueness of ideal fluid motion in those spaces in arbitrary dimension?
Within anisotropic function spaces adapted to hydrodynamics, what is the true regularity of generalized minimal flows?

For a compact Riemannian three-manifold M, can one quantify how the L2 exponential map on D_mu^s(M) fails to be a Fredholm map, for example by measuring the noncompact part of the operator that appears in its derivative?
accepted.context_brief: Fredholm failure of the L2 exponential map

accepted.question_text: For two-dimensional hydrodynamics on D_mu^s(M), what is the order of the first conjugate point along any L2 geodesic from the identity, and is the existence of conjugate points related to Arnold's stability criterion for stationary flows on M?

For a geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M) on a compact two-dimensional manifold, with absolute complexity C defined via products of small exponential-map neighborhoods of the identity, can one prove that C(gamma(t)) is bounded above exponentially in time by a constant of the form exp(t||dot gamma(0)||_{H^s})?
accepted.context_brief: Exponential upper bound on flow complexity

accepted.question_text: For a typical geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M), where typical means that the exceptional set of initial velocities has infinite codimension, can one show that the absolute complexity grows linearly, with C(gamma(t)) comparable to t?

Can the aging of an ideal fluid be quantified from its velocity field, for example by constructing a continuous Lyapunov function on the velocity space whose value is nondecreasing along Euler solutions and is constant only on a slim subset?

For an ideal fluid in a periodic channel T x (0,a), with initial velocity C^1-close to a plane-parallel flow whose velocity profile is increasing and convex, and with an initial vorticity level line containing a kink, can one prove that the kink persists under the Euler evolution?

For entropy notions of compact sets and probability measures in metric or Hilbert spaces, including H_epsilon, H_{epsilon,delta}, tilde H_epsilon, and tilde H_{epsilon,delta}, what are their properties and how are they related?
accepted.context_brief: Entropy functions for sets and measures

accepted.question_text: For two-dimensional Euler solutions, can one explain why the epsilon-entropy of an ensemble of velocity fields appears to decrease at large times, even though the full fluid phase space also includes particle positions and is not simply the velocity space?

Can one prove non-integrability of the two-dimensional Euler equation, in the sense that the equation fails at least one appropriate notion of integrability for infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems despite having Casimirs and a Lax-type form?

Can one justify the numerically observed phenomenon that integrable point-vortex configurations are attractors for two-dimensional Euler flows with generic smooth initial vorticity and small numerical viscosity, and design a dissipation model for 2D Euler that yields such integrable large-time dynamics?

For small numbers of point vortices, can one systematically study their motion and bifurcations on manifolds such as half-planes, quarter-planes, hemispheres, quarter-spheres, disks, tori, cylinders, and half-cylinders?

For point vortices on non-orientable surfaces, can one study the first non-integrable small-vortex cases and describe both the full set of Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations for area-preserving diffeomorphism groups, analogously to the orientable case?

Does the three-dimensional Euler equation have wandering solutions, analogous to Nadirashvili's two-dimensional annulus example in which a neighborhood of an initial condition never returns sufficiently close after some time?
Can the smoothness restrictions in KAM-based non-transitivity and non-mixing results for the three-dimensional Euler equation be relaxed, proving those dynamical properties in full generality?

For an integrable system on a compact 2n-dimensional manifold with n independent commuting first integrals almost everywhere, how wild can the dynamics be on singular submanifolds where the integrals become dependent? What constraints does integrability impose, and can chaotic behavior occur on a tiny singular submanifold?
accepted.context_brief: Chaos on singular parts of integrable systems

accepted.question_text: For steady incompressible Euler fields, especially in three dimensions where generic steady fields have regular torus or annulus fibrations but Beltrami fields can have complicated topology, what is the right notion of a typical steady field and of genericity?

Can one find a hierarchy of higher helicity invariants for divergence-free vector fields such that, when all previous invariants vanish, the first nonzero invariant gives a lower bound for the field's energy?
For divergence-free vector fields undergoing magnetic relaxation, can one describe and analyze the relaxation process to an equilibrium, possibly a nonsmooth equilibrium?

Can one derive a direct reduction from the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation to the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation through singular solutions, without passing through the localized induction approximation? Similarly, can compressible Euler equations be reduced from three dimensions to singular solutions supported on one-dimensional submanifolds?
accepted.context_brief: Singular reductions of NLS and compressible Euler

accepted.question_text: For shape spaces of closed hypersurfaces bounding the same volume, equipped with hydrodynamically induced nonlocal H^{-1/2} metrics arising from dynamic boundaries or vortex sheets, can one describe their differential geometry?

Can the Madelung-transform results identifying symplectomorphism and Kahler map structures be extended to wave functions with zeros on M, and can the quantization-condition controversy be explained through the momentum map for the semidirect product of diffeomorphisms and smooth functions?
Can the correspondence between bouncing droplets in vibrating liquids and quantum particles be explained by combining averaging with the Madelung transform?

In a countable-ball mechanical model for direct cascade, can one choose family sizes n_i, masses m_i, and radii r_i so that energy cascades toward increasing family index and dissipates from the system, and can one identify corresponding structures in an actual three-dimensional fluid?

In an infinite mechanical model intended to produce a direct energy cascade through families of balls, can energy dissipation be introduced in a natural way without explicitly adding friction or an artificial far-away energy sink?
accepted.context_brief: Natural dissipation in direct cascade models

accepted.question_text: For the proposed infinite-chamber mechanical model of inverse cascade, is there an analogous mechanism in real hydrodynamics, and can the parameters n_i, m_i, and r_i be chosen so that the apparatus transfers energy to the first few chambers as intended?
